Google Cast V2 Windows implementation

The 32 Java files in su.litvak.chromecast.api.v2 are from the published
de.sfuhrm:chromecast-java-api-v2:0.12.20 source artifact, SHA-256
312fd605cd0ef4cfff54bbcd49cb48e9df2c01342d61192f757d376d6b178ad3.
The source archive, original per-file hashes and Windows changes are retained here.
Channel.java, ChromeCast.java and ChromeCasts.java contain marked Windows changes
for device authentication, bounded IO, cancellation and payload redaction.
The original Apache-2.0 copyright notices are retained in all original files.
Do not also depend on the original binary artifact: that would duplicate classes.

Open Screen commit 45c685cee0b522a7bb578ce5adcc696eeacf0f0c provides the actual
device-auth proto, channel framing, certificate policy and two pinned Google roots.
The official proto is compiled with protoc 4.33.2 (Java lite) into package
openscreen.cast.proto. The JVM certificate verifier is a new Windows binding of
this contract. Original Open Screen files and BSD-3-Clause license are retained.
The Cast and Eureka DER resource bytes exactly match their original C++ headers.

The runtime authenticates the supplied device chain against only those two roots,
checks key use/strength/dates/path constraints and the nonce plus current TLS DER
signature before CONNECT/LAUNCH/LOAD. It uses Open Screen's optional-CRL baseline;
it does not fetch external AIA or install trust anchors in the operating system.
Unlike the official legacy sender defaults, this port requires the response nonce.
RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 with SHA-256/SHA-1 is implemented; RSASSA-PSS is rejected.
These compatibility differences and real-device testing remain open parity work.

Runtime dependencies are fixed separately: JmDNS 3.6.3, protobuf-javalite 4.33.2,
Jackson annotations 2.20 / core and databind 2.20.0, SLF4J API 2.0.17.
Their Maven URLs and artifact hashes are recorded in SOURCES.json. Available
artifact license and notice texts accompany this file and are bundled under
resources/licenses/google-cast-v2. The Java fork and Open Screen license texts
are included there too.

The tests open only task-owned loopback TLS sockets and advertise a unique mDNS
fixture on the selected loopback interface. Synthetic private material exists
only in src/test/resources/google-cast-v2-fixture and is excluded from main.
The fixed test clock makes certificate boundary cases repeatable over time.
Protocol fixtures are actual socket tests, not proof of physical receiver success.
No physical Google Cast device has been tested by this implementation.
